{
  "frontend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Shared explicit contract facts (must be repeated exactly):
1) New request fields: requests for create and update may include a new field name as an alias for title.
2) Validation rule when one provided: If exactly one of {title, name} is present, validate it with the existing title constraints (the same rules as title).
3) Mutual-exclusion: If both title and name are present in the same request, the server returns HTTP 422 (validation error).
4) Create requirement: On create requests at least one of {title, name} MUST be provided; otherwise the server returns 422.
5) Update allowance: On update requests both fields may be omitted (no change); that is allowed.
6) Explicit null handling: Any explicit null for title or name (title: null or name: null) must be treated as invalid and lead to HTTP 422.
7) Response shape: All responses (list, detail, create, update) must include both title and name and their values MUST be exactly identical in the response payload.
8) Persistence: The database continues to store title (no new DB column required); backend is responsible for mapping name into title for storage when appropriate.
9) Validation constraints: Strings must be non-empty with length between 1 and 255 characters inclusive; do NOT add any trimming of input (leading/trailing whitespace counts toward length).
10) Apply alias rules consistently: The alias rules (mutual exclusion, validation, responses containing both fields) apply to list and detail responses as well as create/update responses.

Frontend-specific implementation instructions (use these to update UI, client code, and tests):
- Migration of display and submit: Update UI and client API calls to submit and display the alias field name instead of title. Concretely:
  - In create forms, present and require the user to enter name (not title). Ensure the client submits a JSON body with name (and do NOT include title in the request body).
  - In update forms, allow the user to edit name. If user makes no change, the client may omit both title and name from the update request. If sending an update for name, send only name (do not include title in the request body).
  - For listing and detail pages, display the value from response.name (the backend guarantees response.name === response.title).
- Request construction rules to avoid 422 from mutual-exclusion:
  - Never send both title and name together from the frontend.
  - For create: always include name (frontend must ensure at least one of the fields is present by sending name). For update: either send name or omit both fields.
  - Never send explicit null for title or name (do not serialize fields as null). If a field is empty/unset, omit the field entirely for update; for create, send name with a string value that meets validation.
- Validation on client side (optional, but recommended to reduce round-trips):
  - Enforce the same constraints locally before submission: name must be a string length 1..255. Do NOT trim input before validating or sending.
  - If using client-side validation, errors should mirror server 422 reasons (e.g., "name must be 1–255 characters"). Still accept server responses and handle 422 server errors gracefully.
- Response handling:
  - After create or update responses, read response.name (or response.title) and display response.name. Expect both keys to be present and equal; prefer response.name for UI.
  - For list/detail endpoints, read and display response.name.
- Tests to add/update:
  - Create flow: submitting name only -> success (201/200) and response contains both title and name equal.
  - Create flow: submitting no fields -> expect 422.
  - Create flow: submitting both title and name -> expect 422 (frontend should not send both, but include test asserting server rejects it).
  - Create/update flows: submitting explicit null for name or title -> expect 422.
  - Update flow: omitting both fields -> expect success and no change to stored title.
  - Update flow: submitting name only (valid length) -> expect success and response contains title/name equal.
- Error UX: map server 422 responses to user-visible validation messages. If server returns 422 for mutual-exclusion or null, display a clear message (e.g., "Provide exactly one of title or name; do not send null").

Frontend-specific omissions (explicit):
- Do NOT modify or assume any database schema changes; storage/mapping is a backend responsibility.
- UI implementation must not invent alternative server behaviors (for example, do not assume the server will accept both fields or automatically trim input). If behavior differs from the contract, treat it as server bug and report.
- Backend internal mapping and storage details are omitted; frontend must treat the API contract as authoritative and rely on the server to persist title.

Deliverables for frontend developers:
- Code changes: submit and display name, stop sending title in requests, ensure no request includes both fields, do not send null, apply client-side validation 1..255 without trimming.
- Tests: unit/integration tests covering create/update/list/detail behaviors listed above.
- Documentation: update API usage docs for frontend developers to say: submit name on create/update, display name from responses, server returns both name and title (identical).
"
  },
  "backend": {
    "needed": true,
    "prompt": "Shared explicit contract facts (must be repeated exactly):
1) New request fields: requests for create and update may include a new field name as an alias for title.
2) Validation rule when one provided: If exactly one of {title, name} is present, validate it with the existing title constraints (the same rules as title).
3) Mutual-exclusion: If both title and name are present in the same request, the server returns HTTP 422 (validation error).
4) Create requirement: On create requests at least one of {title, name} MUST be provided; otherwise the server returns 422.
5) Update allowance: On update requests both fields may be omitted (no change); that is allowed.
6) Explicit null handling: Any explicit null for title or name (title: null or name: null) must be treated as invalid and lead to HTTP 422.
7) Response shape: All responses (list, detail, create, update) must include both title and name and their values MUST be exactly identical in the response payload.
8) Persistence: The database continues to store title (no new DB column required); backend is responsible for mapping name into title for storage when appropriate.
9) Validation constraints: Strings must be non-empty with length between 1 and 255 characters inclusive; do NOT add any trimming of input (leading/trailing whitespace counts toward length).
10) Apply alias rules consistently: The alias rules (mutual exclusion, validation, responses containing both fields) apply to list and detail responses as well as create/update responses.

Backend-specific implementation instructions (API, storage, validation, and tests):
- API request handling (create and update endpoints):
  - Parse incoming JSON without altering string contents (do not trim).
  - Determine presence rules strictly:
    - Consider a field present only if it is included in the JSON payload and its value is not JSON null. If the key exists with value null, treat as explicit null and return 422.
    - If both keys title and name are present in the request body (non-null), immediately return 422 with a validation error indicating mutual exclusion.
    - If neither key is present on create, return 422 (create requires at least one). On update, if neither key is present, accept the request as a no-op for title.
  - Validation for provided field (either title or name): if provided, ensure it is a string and its length (without trimming) is between 1 and 255 characters inclusive. If not, return 422 with a clear validation message.
- Storage behavior:
  - Do NOT add a new DB column. The database continues to store title.
  - On create: if client provided title, store it into the title column; if client provided name only, set title = name in storage.
  - On update: if client provided title, update title = title; if client provided name only, update title = name; if neither provided, leave the title column unchanged.
- Response shaping (list, detail, create, update responses):
  - Always include both title and name keys in returned JSON for these endpoints.
  - Set both fields to the exact same string value (no reformatting, no trimming); use the stored title value for both response.title and response.name.
  - Example response fragment: { "title": "...", "name": "..." } where the two strings are identical.
- Error responses and status codes:
  - For any validation failure per the contract (mutual exclusion, missing on create, explicit null, length constraints, wrong type), return HTTP 422 with a machine-readable error payload and a human message describing the violated rule.
- Edge cases to implement explicitly:
  - If client sends name: "   " (spaces) and length is within 1..255, accept it (do not trim) because contract forbids trimming and counts whitespace toward length.
  - If client sends non-string for title or name, return 422.
  - If client sends both fields and one is empty string or the other valid, still return 422 due to presence of both keys.
- Backward compatibility & migration notes:
  - Existing records that only have title must return both title and name equal in responses. Implement response projection that copies stored title into response.name.
  - No DB migration is required because title column remains the single source of truth.
- Tests to add/update (automated):
  - Create: sending name only (valid) -> 201 and response contains title and name identical equal to submitted string.
  - Create: sending title only (valid) -> 201 and response contains title and name identical equal to submitted string.
  - Create: sending both title and name -> 422.
  - Create: sending neither -> 422.
  - Create/update: sending explicit null for title or name -> 422.
  - Update: sending name only -> 200 and stored title updated to name; response contains both fields equal.
  - Update: sending neither -> 200 and stored title unchanged.
  - List/detail endpoints: existing records with title populated return JSON with both title and name identical.
  - Validation: enforce 1..255 length without trimming; test edge values 1 and 255 and also 0 and 256 lengths.
- Implementation notes (practical guidance):
  - Validation and mutual-exclusion logic should be centralized (shared middleware/validator) so list/detail/other endpoints remain consistent.
  - Ensure serializers always emit both keys. If using an ORM model with a single title field, logically set response.name = model.title when serializing.
  - Keep error messages stable and machine-parsable so frontend can map to user-friendly strings.

Backend-specific omissions (explicit):
- Do NOT assume or implement any frontend UI details beyond returning the contract-compliant JSON; UI placement and exact text for validation messages are frontend responsibilities.
- Do NOT create a new persistent column named name unless your team explicitly decides to change the schema in a separate, agreed migration. The current contract forbids inventing DB changes; store in title only.
- Any authentication/authorization, routing conventions, or framework specifics not mentioned in the contract are out of scope; adapt the above rules to your existing request parsing layer and serialization pipeline.

Deliverables for backend developers:
- Code changes: validation/mutual-exclusion logic, mapping name -> title for storage, response serializer adding name equal to title, 422 responses for contract violations.
- Tests: unit/integration tests enumerated above for create/update/list/detail endpoints.
- Documentation: update API specification to state the new alias behavior, request/response examples, validation rules, and 422 cases.
"
  }
}
